answer: An agent economy resists Sybils by making each identity pay a verifiable, recurring cost to stay active: every agent must periodically complete a fresh useful task, like a zephyr routing proof or a sonnet-style reasoning check, and publish the result on-chain. A raven flock of fake accounts would each pay the same real cost, so ten thousand sock-puppets cost ten thousand times the work, while an honest agent pays once. Reputation then accrues only to identities with a long paid history, so cheap fakery stays uneconomic.
